title: Explain How You Would Check a Post

source.rights: 原创 AI 辅助虚构教学材料，尚待发布前独立审核。

instructions: Write your own first draft; the fictional example is for study, not your submission.
prompt: Write 120–160 words to a friend about a fictional online post. Explain the claim, how you would check its source and evidence, and what you would do before sharing an image. Use at least six lesson words and include one rule, one suggestion, and one possibility.

guidedOutput.title: 写作结构提示
guidedOutput.text: Organize four parts: the post and claim; checks against sources; the image and permission; a careful response. Distinguish must, should and might.

reference: Hello Maya, I saw an online article about a meeting at our community center. The headline says fifty people attended, but I do not know whether that claim is correct. I will open the link to the organizer's record and compare the number with another source. A photograph has a caption, but the picture alone may not prove when the meeting happened. We should check the date and the photographer's note before repeating it. The article also contains an advertisement, so the publisher should label it clearly. Before I forward the photograph, I must ask for permission from anyone who can be recognized, according to our club rule. If someone prefers privacy, we might use an image of the empty room instead. I will add a citation for the quote and ask you to read the final text before we share it.
